chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman al-Daylami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abdullah ibn Qays al-Masir came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'Inform me about the deceased, why is he washed with the washing of major ritual impurity (janabah)?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will not inform you.' So he went out from his presence and met some of the Shias and said to them, 'I wonder at you, O group of Shias! You have accepted the Wilayah of this man and obeyed him, and if he invited you to worship him, you would respond to him; and I asked him about a matter, but there was nothing with him regarding it!'

So when it was the following time, he came to him again and asked him about it, and he said, 'I will not inform you with it.' So Abdullah ibn Qays said to a man from his companions, 'Go to the Shias, be their companion, and display your Wilayah with them in their presence, and curse me and disavow from me. So when it is the time for Hajj, come to me until I hand over to you what you will use for it, and ask them to let you enter upon Muhammad ibn Ali. So when you arrive to him, ask him about the deceased, why is he washed with the washing of janabah.'

So the man went to the Shias and was with them until the time of the season. So he looked at the religion of the people and accepted it with their acceptance, and concealed the matter from Ibn Qays, fearing that he would prevent the Hajj (by not paying for it). So when it was the time for Hajj, he came to him, and he gave him a Hajj (expense), and he went out. So when he arrived in Medina, his companions said to him, 'Stay behind in the house until we mention you to him and ask him for permission for you.'

So when they arrived to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said to them, 'Where is your companion? You have not been just to him.' They said, 'We did not know what your acceptance would be from that.' So he ordered one of those present to bring him. So when he entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said to him, 'Welcome! How is your view of what you are in today, from what you were in beforehand?' So he said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! I wasn't in anything (before).'

So he said, 'You speak the truth. As for your worship in those days, it was lighter upon you than your worship today, because the truth is heavy, and the Satan is allocated with our Shias, because the rest of the people he has sufficed with their selves. I shall be informing you with what Ibn Qays al-Masir said to you, before you even ask me about it; and relating the matter in presenting it to him, it is up to you, if you so desire it, inform him, and if you so desire, do not inform him.'

Indeed, Allah the Exalted created creators. So whenever He intends to create a creature, He commands them, and they take from the dust which He said in His Book: 'From it We created you and into it We shall send you back and from it will We bring you out once again.' So the seed is kneaded with that dust from which he is created, after it has settled in the womb for forty nights. So when four months are completed for it, they say, 'O Lord! What is that?' So He commands them with whatever He intends, whether a male or a female, white or black. So when the soul comes out from the body, this exact seed comes out from it, as it was before, whether young or old, male or female. Thus, it is due to that, the deceased is washed with the washing of janabah.'
So the man said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! No, by Allah! I will not inform Ibn Qays al-Masir with this, ever!' So he said, 'That is up to you.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the deceased washed with the washing of janabah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi addresses the theological rationale behind washing the deceased with the same ritual as major impurity (janabah), linking it to the physical origin of the body from earth. Imam Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (or Abu Ja'far, depending on the specific narration variant) explains that since humans are created from clay and to it they return, the body retains a connection to its elemental source, necessitating purification akin to janabah. The narrative highlights the Shia practice of testing the depth of faith among companions, as the envoy deliberately concealed the answer to prevent Ibn Qays from becoming overly attached to the Imam's authority.
